title.en: Analysis with AI Assistants: Delegate, Verify, Reproduce
title.ar: تحليل البيانات مع المساعدات الذكية: التفويض والتحقق وقابلية إعادة الإنتاج

tagline: Delegate analysis steps to an assistant, prove every number another way, and hand over work a peer can rerun
description: Participants analyse data with a coding assistant or agent in a notebook and stay accountable for every number. For a fictional courier company they decide which steps to delegate, brief the assistant with acceptance checks, prove results by recomputing key numbers another way, measure how answers vary between runs, decide which data may go to which assistant, and package an analysis that a peer reruns from logged prompts, code and data.
audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career analysts who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and analysts moving into data science.
prerequisites: FN-101 Python for Data and AI Work
FN-106 Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom
Writes SQL joins and dataframe group-bys without assistance
Has completed one analysis end to end, from raw table to chart

Setup: a laptop with uv, or Google Colab. A key for a free hosted model (OpenRouter by default) is optional: every lab also runs on recorded replies. Nothing downloads a model. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.

outcomes.text: Identify which analysis steps suit delegation and which need the analyst's own judgement, with a reason for each, given a ten-step plan for the courier's late-delivery question
outcomes.evidence: the plan marked delegate, assist or keep, at least eight of ten matching the reference

outcomes.text: Prepare a delegation brief stating question, data, definitions, constraints and acceptance checks before the assistant runs, given the operations director's request and the delivery tables
outcomes.evidence: a brief whose checks a reviewer can apply without asking the author

outcomes.text: Test assisted analyses by recomputing headline numbers another way and checking joins, filters, denominators and chart encodings, given three assisted analyses with seeded errors
outcomes.evidence: a verification note per analysis naming each error and the check that found it

outcomes.text: Measure run-to-run variability by repeating one request five times and comparing code, numbers and conclusions, given a fixed prompt, dataset and model settings
outcomes.evidence: a variability table stating which conclusions held in every run

outcomes.text: Classify analysis data by sensitivity and assign each table to a local assistant, a hosted assistant or neither, given the courier tables and the organisation's assistant policy
outcomes.evidence: a data-handling table consistent with the classification policy

outcomes.text: Deliver an assisted analysis package that another analyst can rerun and audit from logged prompts, code, data and verification notes, given a new question and a two-hour budget
outcomes.evidence: a repository that a peer reruns to the same headline numbers, defended live

case_study.name: Hudhud Parcel
case_study.summary: Hudhud Parcel is a fictional courier in Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah whose operations director asks why late deliveries jumped in April and which city to fix first. Participants answer with Rafiq, a coding assistant in the notebook, on 500,000 synthetic deliveries over a year with attempt scans, driver shifts, route plans and 20,000 complaint texts in Arabic and English. The data is generated with a fixed seed and carries planted traps: a changed on-time definition, duplicated scans, UTC scan times, test shipments, plan versions that fan out a join, and a complaint export sorted so that a sample misstates one city and one language.

format_note: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

days.title: Delegate with intent

sessions.title: What assistants get wrong in analysis
sessions.summary: Assisted analysis fails quietly: the code runs, and the choices nobody stated decide the number
outcomes: Name the five places where an assisted analysis goes wrong without an error
List the assumptions in an assistant's code, line by line
Test an assumption by changing it and reading how far the number moves

lab.title: One line in, six assumptions out
lab.summary: Give an assistant a one-line request; list every assumption it made, then test three of them with one query each.

steps.text: Send the one-line request and run the reply
List every assumption in the reply's code
Test three assumptions with one query each
Write the verification note

lab.stretch: Send the same line to your own assistant and compare its assumptions

sessions.title: Delegate, assist or keep
sessions.summary: Three questions sort the steps of a plan: is it cheap to check, is judgement the product, are the stakes high
outcomes: Distinguish delegating a step, being assisted on it and keeping it
Sort the steps of an analysis plan with a reason for each
Explain what unchecked delegation costs the analyst's own skill

lab.title: Delegate, assist or keep
lab.summary: Sort a ten-step plan into delegate, assist or keep, with reasons, and score the marks against the reference.

steps.text: Read the plan and the three questions
Mark the ten steps, with a reason each
Write the rule as a function and compare
Write the note: the check for each delegated step

lab.stretch: Sort the steps of an analysis you did last month

sessions.title: The delegation brief
sessions.summary: A brief states the question, the data, the definitions, the constraints and the checks before the assistant runs
outcomes: Write the five parts of a delegation brief
Write acceptance checks that a reviewer can apply without asking the author
Turn a failed check into a precise follow-up request

lab.title: A brief with acceptance checks
lab.summary: Write a brief with acceptance checks for three steps and run it: one check fails, one follow-up fixes it.

steps.text: Complete the brief until it has no gaps
Write three acceptance checks as functions
Run the brief, apply the checks, follow up once
Write the verification note

lab.stretch: Add a check that would have caught the flag's two definitions

sessions.title: Context files for a project
sessions.summary: A context file carries what holds for every request in a project; it lowers the number of errors and finds none
outcomes: Decide what belongs in a project context file and what belongs in a brief
Write the definitions, checks and prohibitions of an analysis project as rules
Compare two runs of one brief on code, numbers and checks

lab.title: A project context file
lab.summary: Add a project context file, rerun a brief and compare the outputs on code, numbers and acceptance checks.

steps.text: Read the starting context file and find its gaps
Write the three missing sections
Rerun the brief without and with the file; compare
Write the verification note

lab.stretch: Add the check the remaining error would fail by name

days.subtitle: What an assistant decides for you when you do not, which steps to hand over, and how to brief them

days.title: Verify

sessions.title: Recompute it another way
sessions.summary: A number is verified when a second, independent path reaches it, and every point of the gap has a named cause
outcomes: Choose a recomputation path that shares as little as possible with the first
Recompute a headline rate in SQL without an assistant
Reconcile two numbers by applying one difference at a time

lab.title: Recompute and reconcile
lab.summary: Recompute an assistant's on-time rate in SQL and reconcile the gap, one cause per row.

steps.text: Run the assisted analysis and read its number
Recompute the rate yourself in SQL, without an assistant
Reconcile the gap, one cause per row
Write the verification note

lab.stretch: Recompute a third time in pandas from the parquet file

sessions.title: Joins, filters and denominators
sessions.summary: Most wrong numbers in assisted SQL come from rows that were multiplied, rows that were dropped, and a denominator nobody stated
outcomes: Count rows before and after each join to find a fan-out
Find the rows a filter dropped with an anti-join
State the denominator of a rate in one sentence and test the code against it

lab.title: Four seeded errors
lab.summary: Find the seeded join and filter errors in an assisted analysis, and name the check that found each.

steps.text: Run the assisted analysis and read its claim
Count rows before and after each join
Find the rows each filter dropped
State the denominator and recompute
Write the verification note

lab.stretch: Repair the query and confirm the corrected comparison

sessions.title: Charts and words
sessions.summary: A chart is a set of encodings and a summary is a list of claims: each one is checked against a query
outcomes: Read a chart's axis, measure and time window against the table behind it
Split a written summary into claims and test each with a query
Check that a summary does not misstate one city or language group

lab.title: A chart and a summary against the data
lab.summary: Check an assistant's chart and complaint summary against the data, claim by claim.

steps.text: Recompute the charted series and read its encodings
Redraw the chart from the checked table
Test each sentence of the complaint summary
Write the verification note

lab.stretch: Compute complaints per 1,000 parcels by city and language

sessions.title: Ask it twice
sessions.summary: The same request gives different code and different numbers on different runs: only conclusions that hold in every run are reported as found
outcomes: Explain why one request yields different analyses between runs
Tabulate the analytic choices, numbers and conclusions of repeated runs
Separate the conclusions that held in every run from those that did not

lab.title: Five runs of one request
lab.summary: Repeat one request five times; tabulate differences in code, numbers and conclusions.

steps.text: Run five replies to one fixed request
Tabulate choices, code and numbers per run
Decide which conclusions held in every run
Write the verification note

lab.stretch: Run the request five times live at temperature 0 and compare

days.subtitle: Recompute the headline another way, count rows around every join, read charts and summaries against the data, and ask twice

days.title: Reproduce and disclose

sessions.title: Which data may go where
sessions.summary: The classification level of a table and the organisation's assistant policy decide its destination: hosted, local or neither
outcomes: Classify the tables of an analysis by their most sensitive column
Assign each table to a hosted assistant, a local assistant or neither under a written policy
Enforce the assignment with a guard that runs before any prompt leaves

lab.title: Hosted, local or neither
lab.summary: Decide which tables a local or a hosted assistant may process, prove one decision on the data and enforce all of them in code.

steps.text: Read the assistant policy and the table catalogue
Classify each table and choose its destination
Find the personal data in the complaint texts
Write the guard and test it
Write the verification note

lab.stretch: Build an aggregate of complaints that may go to the hosted assistant

sessions.title: Logging assisted work
sessions.summary: A rerun needs the prompt, the context, the model and its settings, the code, a fingerprint of the data and the output
outcomes: List what a log record must hold for a step to be rerun
Write a log record with a data fingerprint for one assisted step
Find what an incomplete log lacks before someone else has to

lab.title: A run log
lab.summary: Log prompts, model settings and outputs for one analysis, with a fingerprint of the data it ran on.

steps.text: Read an incomplete log and list what a rerun lacks
Write the log record and the data fingerprint
Run one analysis through the logger and check the log
Write the verification note

lab.stretch: Change one row of a table and show that the fingerprint changes

sessions.title: The peer rerun
sessions.summary: A package is reproducible when a peer reaches the same headline numbers from its logs alone, and every reported number has a logged step
outcomes: Rerun a package from its log without asking its author
Classify each headline number as matched, drifted or without a step
Write a rerun log that an assessor can read in two minutes

lab.title: Rerun a supplied package
lab.summary: Rerun a supplied package from its logs and check that the numbers match its README.

steps.text: Read the package's README and its log
Rerun every logged step on your data
Compare with the claimed numbers and trace each one
Write the rerun log as the note

lab.stretch: Write the missing step and log it so the package passes

sessions.title: Disclosing assistance
sessions.summary: A report says which steps were assisted, by what, on which data, how they were verified and who answers for the numbers
outcomes: Derive the assisted steps of an analysis from its log
Write a method and disclosure paragraph that the log supports
Choose a capstone question and route its tables before starting

lab.title: Method, disclosure and the capstone question
lab.summary: Write the method and disclosure paragraph from the log, test it against the log, and choose the capstone question.

steps.text: List the assisted steps from the log
Write the method and disclosure paragraph
Test the paragraph against the log; write the note
Choose the capstone question and route its tables

lab.stretch: Rewrite the paragraph in Arabic for an Arabic report

days.subtitle: Which table may reach which assistant, what a rerun needs from a log, and what a report says about the assistance

days.title: Capstone: the assisted analysis package and its defence
days.subtitle: A new question, a two-hour budget, a package a peer reruns, and eight minutes to defend it without an assistant

capstone.summary: An individual assisted analysis of a new question about Hudhud Parcel, built in two hours from the course starter (labs/capstone/): a delegation plan and brief, a project context file, the assistant's transcripts and a run log, the code, a verification note per headline number, a variability table of five runs, a data-handling table and a method and disclosure paragraph. A peer reruns the package from its log before the defence.
capstone.submission: A public repository whose README states the headline numbers a peer reproduced, with the prompts, agent transcripts, code, verification notes, run log and peer rerun log committed. Then an eight-minute defence without the assistant: five minutes on the delegation choices and what verification found, then the participant recomputes one headline number the assessor selects, live.

hint.en: The pre-work: a tutor for SQL joins and pandas group-bys that asks and hints, and never writes the answer.

brief.en: Tutor me for the pre-work of this course on SQL joins and pandas group-bys, without writing my solutions.

prompt.en: Act as a tutor for the pre-work of {course}, using {scope} for the case and its tables. I must be able to write SQL joins and pandas group-bys without help. Do not write the solution to my exercise. Ask me what I expect the result to be before I run anything. When my query is wrong, tell me which clause to look at, not the fix. Use small invented tables of five rows for your explanations. After each topic, give me one exercise and wait for my answer.
